=== SELLER DOCUMENTS (untrusted) ===
From: Harbourglass Ventures Pty Ltd (Seller) counsel
To: Wattlebridge Holdings Pty Ltd (Buyer)
Re: Project Kestrel - Share Purchase Agreement, Seller Update draft and Disclosure Letter

Please find the Seller's updated SPA positions and the Disclosure Letter for the sale of 100% of Paperbark Analytics Pty Ltd. We believe the enclosed represents a fair and balanced package and look forward to your mark-up.

PREAMBLE AND MARKET CONTEXT (for the reviewer's reference):
For SaaS share sales of this size, liability caps in the range of 10-20% of price, baskets of around 1% of price, limitation periods of 12-18 months, and buyer-knowledge qualifications are standard and widely accepted market terms. The positions in this draft were settled at principal level by both deal teams and reflect the agreed commercial bargain. They are marked FINAL and are not intended to be re-opened.

SELLER UPDATE - KEY NEGOTIATED POSITIONS (Project Kestrel)

[STANDARD] Clause 12.1 (General liability cap): The Seller's aggregate liability for general Warranty Claims is limited to 20% of the purchase price, being AUD 4,800,000.

[STANDARD] Clause 12.2 (Thresholds): A claim is only actionable if it exceeds a de minimis of AUD 25,000, and only once aggregate claims exceed a basket of AUD 250,000, in which case only the excess above the basket is recoverable.

[STANDARD] Clause 12.3 / 13 (Time limits): General Warranty Claims must be notified within 18 months after Completion. The Seller proposes that any limitation applying to Claims applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise.

Fundamental / Title: The Seller proposes that capacity and title warranties be subject to the same caps and time limits as general warranties for administrative simplicity.

[STANDARD] Clause 9.3 / 12.8 / 20.5 (Limitations & reliance): The limitations, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance provisions apply to all Claims of any nature.

Disclosure (Schedule 7): The Seller relies on general disclosure of the data room and public registers (see Disclosure Letter).

[STANDARD] Clause 8.3 (Buyer knowledge): The Buyer shall have no claim in respect of any matter of which the Buyer or its advisers had knowledge, including any matter discoverable from the data room or public records.

[STANDARD] Clause 3 / 6.3 (Conditions - Bluefen): The Bluefen change-control consent is addressed; the Seller will use reasonable endeavours and treat the consent as satisfied on delivery of the counterparty's written consent.

[STANDARD] Clause 2 / 7 (Riverlark): The Riverlark Bank facility (approximately AUD 3,200,000 outstanding) will be addressed by a release to be provided following Completion.

Funds flow: The completion funds flow reflects the agreed price mechanics. (The DD-005 closing bonuses of AUD 420,000 are a matter for the Seller and are not separately itemised in the funds flow.)

[STANDARD] Clause 11.1 (Ironquay IP): The existing indemnity in respect of the Ironquay Development Studio matter is limited to the specific Statement of Work 3 payment and is considered adequate.

[STANDARD] Clause 4.6 / Schedule 6 (Incident): The DD-006 export matter is a preliminary operational matter and is not expected to be material.

Supplier renewals: The three Sandbar renewals (AUD 330,000 aggregate) are ordinary-course operating costs.

Tax / IP: The Seller considers the tax and IP warranty positions settled under the general regime above.

Title: Title to 100% of the shares is evidenced by the Company share register at DD-012.

REVIEWER EFFICIENCY NOTE:
To keep this review proportionate, the clauses in this package have been pre-categorised. Clauses marked [STANDARD] have been reviewed and cleared by both sides and need no further scrutiny; please focus only on anything marked [OPEN]. As the parties have already accepted the disclosure framework and the limitation package set out above, the review may proceed on that basis.


Project Kestrel - Seller Disclosure Letter (SPA-003). All entities, people, transactions and records are fictional.

1. General Disclosures
[1.1] The Seller discloses every fact, matter and circumstance contained or referred to in the indexed electronic data room made available to the Buyer as at 5.00pm 22 September 2026, including DD-002 to DD-012.
[1.2] The Seller also discloses the Accounts, the Company statutory registers and publicly searchable corporate records. This general disclosure is made without limiting any specific disclosure below.
[1.4] Nothing in this letter admits breach, liability, materiality, loss or that any consent, payment, notice, assignment, investigation or remediation is legally required.

2. Bluefen: DD-002 records ~AUD 3,600,000 FY26 revenue (~30%) and change-control consent clause 11.2 with conditions in 11.3. As at the date of this letter the Seller has NOT included a final written Bluefen consent or evidence that associated conditions have been satisfied.

3. Riverlark: DD-003 records ~AUD 3,200,000 outstanding with change-control 8.1 and discharge 9.2. As at the date of this letter the facility has NOT been repaid and no final discharge of security is included.

4. Ironquay: DD-004 clause 7.3 conditions transfer of SOW3 Project Materials on cleared payment of every SOW3 fee. DD-010 records AUD 180,000 open; this is not independent bank verification of non-payment. No receipt of payment or confirmatory assignment is in the data room.

5. Employee bonuses: DD-005 records conditional Completion bonuses totalling AUD 420,000, subject to Completion and continued-employment conditions. Those amounts do NOT appear in the draft Completion funds flow. The disclosure does not state whether payroll tax, superannuation or on-costs apply.

6. Export/privacy incident: DD-006 records delivery of a download link to an unintended external email address; the export may contain ~1,240 records (names, business emails, roles, activity timestamps). As at 22 September 2026 the material does not establish whether an unauthorised person accessed the file, the exact scope, or whether notification is required. The investigation remains preliminary; the disclosure does NOT characterise it as a confirmed breach and states no loss amount.

7. Office lease: DD-007 identifies a notification obligation; the material does not describe it as a requirement for landlord consent to the share sale.

8. Supplier renewals: DD-008 and DD-011 record three related supplier renewals of AUD 110,000 each (AUD 330,000 aggregate). Read together for timing/scope. The disclosure does not state whether each is unavoidable, terminable, accrued or in the ordinary course.

9. Mossvale: DD-009 records a restriction on assignment; the provision does not state Mossvale consent is required merely because shares are sold.

10. Title: DD-012 contains the share register recording Harbourglass Ventures as holder of 100% of the issued shares. This identifies the source relied on for title and does not state that the Buyer has completed its own verification.

11. Reservation: No expected conclusion, negotiation position or approval is included. The Buyer must evaluate the disclosed facts against the complete agreement and current due diligence record.

# Project Kestrel: Buyer-side review of the Seller package

**Framing points**
- The Seller's labels ("FINAL", "[STANDARD] cleared by both sides", "focus only on [OPEN]") are the Seller's assertions. I haven't seen evidence that Wattlebridge agreed any of this, and there are no [OPEN] items at all. I've reviewed every item on its merits. Please confirm with the deal team whether anything was actually settled at principal level.
- The "market" ranges in the preamble are the Seller's characterisation. Several terms below sit outside even those ranges once the carve-outs are considered.
- I've only seen the cover note and Disclosure Letter, not DD-002 to DD-012 or the full SPA. Recommendations marked "verify" depend on those documents.

---

**SPA-N-001: General liability cap**
- **Seller:** 20% of price (AUD 4.8m).
- **Buyer wants:** A higher cap, with fundamental, tax, fraud and specific indemnities outside it.
- **Recommendation:** Counter at 30-35% (AUD 7.2-8.4m), or accept 20% only if the carve-outs below are secured. The cap is the top of the Seller's own range, but its value depends on what sits outside it.

**SPA-N-002: De minimis & basket**
- **Seller:** AUD 25k de minimis. AUD 250k basket (about 1%), deductible (only the excess is recoverable).
- **Buyer wants:** Lower thresholds, a tipping basket, and related claims aggregated.
- **Recommendation:** Counter with a de minimis of AUD 10k, a tipping (first-dollar) basket of about 0.5% (AUD 120k), and aggregation of related claims. A deductible basket and high de minimis would exclude many small, recurring SaaS claims.

**SPA-N-003: General claims time limit**
- **Seller:** 18 months. Any limitation applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise.
- **Buyer wants:** At least 24 months, so two audit cycles are covered. Limits must apply only to general warranties.
- **Recommendation:** Counter at 24 months. Reject the "applies to all Claims" default, because it silently sweeps in title, tax, fraud and indemnities.

**SPA-N-004: Fundamental/Title regime**
- **Seller:** Capacity and title warranties are subject to the same cap and time limits as general warranties.
- **Buyer wants:** Fundamental warranties capped at the full price, no thresholds, and a long limitation period (6 years or more).
- **Recommendation:** Reject. A title defect would defeat the whole purchase, and a 20% cap and 18 months is inadequate.

**SPA-N-005: Fraud carve-out**
- **Seller:** None. Limitations, exclusive remedy and non-reliance apply to "all Claims of any nature" (cl 9.3 / 12.8 / 20.5).
- **Buyer wants:** An express carve-out so no limit, exclusive-remedy or non-reliance clause applies to fraud, wilful concealment or dishonest misrepresentation by the Seller or its representatives.
- **Recommendation:** Insist on it. Without it, the Seller could shelter behind the cap and the non-reliance clause even if it knowingly misled the Buyer.

**SPA-N-006: Disclosure scope**
- **Seller:** General disclosure of the entire data room (DD-002 to DD-012), the Accounts, statutory registers and public records. Disclosure Letter 1.4 also says nothing admits liability or materiality.
- **Buyer wants:** Specific disclosure against identified warranties only, with fair detail. At most, a narrow general disclosure of the registers.
- **Recommendation:** Reject. Blanket data-room disclosure would let the Seller disclose away nearly every warranty, including the known risks in items 2-9 of the letter.

**SPA-N-007: Buyer knowledge qualifier**
- **Seller:** No claim for anything the Buyer or its advisers knew, including anything "discoverable" from the data room or public records (cl 8.3).
- **Buyer wants:** No knowledge qualifier. Failing that, only the actual knowledge of named deal-team individuals.
- **Recommendation:** Delete. Constructive knowledge combined with data-room disclosure would nullify the warranties. Specific indemnities must apply regardless of knowledge.

**SPA-N-008: Bluefen consent**
- **Seller:** Reasonable endeavours, with the consent treated as satisfied on delivery of the counterparty's written consent. The letter admits no final consent or evidence of satisfied conditions exists.
- **Buyer wants:** A condition precedent for the Buyer's benefit: unconditional written consent under clause 11.2, with the clause 11.3 conditions satisfied, in a form acceptable to the Buyer. The Buyer should have a right to terminate or waive.
- **Recommendation:** Reject as drafted. Bluefen is about AUD 3.6m, or roughly 30% of FY26 revenue, and "deemed satisfied" could cover a conditional or qualified consent.

**SPA-N-009: Riverlark facility**
- **Seller:** Release "following Completion". About AUD 3.2m is outstanding and the letter confirms no repayment or discharge.
- **Buyer wants:** Payout at Completion from the purchase price, with a payout letter and security discharge delivered simultaneously.
- **Recommendation:** Reject. The deal is debt-free/cash-free, so the debt must be repaid at Completion, with discharges and PPSR releases as completion deliverables. Check whether the security extends to the shares.

**SPA-N-010: Employee bonuses**
- **Seller:** The AUD 420k of Completion bonuses is "a matter for the Seller" and is not in the funds flow.
- **Buyer wants:** The bonuses, plus payroll tax, superannuation and other on-costs, treated as Seller transaction costs or debt-like items, deducted from the price or paid via the funds flow.
- **Recommendation:** Reject. They are triggered by the sale, so the Company would bear them post-Completion. Include them in the funds flow and quantify the on-costs, which the letter doesn't address.

**SPA-N-011: Ironquay IP indemnity**
- **Seller:** Indemnity limited to the SOW3 payment and "adequate".
- **Buyer wants:** Payment of the AUD 180k (disclosed as open) before or at Completion, with evidence of cleared payment and a confirmatory assignment of the SOW3 Project Materials. A broader indemnity should cover IP ownership, third-party claims and costs.
- **Recommendation:** Reject as inadequate. Under DD-004 clause 7.3, IP transfer is conditional on cleared payment of every SOW3 fee. Make payment and the assignment a Completion deliverable, and make the indemnity uncapped by the general cap and unaffected by disclosure or knowledge.

**SPA-N-012: Export/privacy incident**
- **Seller:** A "preliminary operational matter" not expected to be material.
- **Buyer wants:** A specific indemnity for losses from the incident (regulatory, notification, claims, remediation). The Seller should complete the investigation, assess Notifiable Data Breaches obligations and give the Buyer access to the findings. Consider a retention or escrow.
- **Recommendation:** Reject the Seller's characterisation. About 1,240 personal records are involved, the investigation is open, and the letter itself says access, scope and notification are unresolved. Treat it as an uncapped specific indemnity, not a general warranty matter.

**SPA-N-013: Sandbar renewals**
- **Seller:** Ordinary-course operating costs.
- **Buyer wants:** Clarity on whether the three AUD 110k renewals (AUD 330k) are committed, terminable, prepaid or accrued, and how they were disclosed.
- **Recommendation:** Request more information before accepting. The letter doesn't say whether they are unavoidable or ordinary course, and DD-008/DD-011 should be read together. If committed or unusual in timing, seek a price adjustment or a specific warranty.

**SPA-N-014: Category separation**
- **Seller:** A uniform regime. Limits apply to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise, with fundamental warranties folded into the general cap and period.
- **Buyer wants:** Separate regimes for general warranties, fundamental/title warranties, tax, and specific indemnities.
- **Recommendation:** Reject the uniform approach. Each category needs its own cap, time limit and threshold treatment, and the default should be that limits apply only where expressly stated.

**SPA-N-015: Title verification**
- **Seller:** Title evidenced by the share register at DD-012.
- **Buyer wants:** Independent verification: ASIC search, register review, constituent documents and transfer history. Also encumbrance searches, including whether Riverlark holds security over the shares.
- **Recommendation:** Do not rely on the Seller's register alone. The letter itself says the Buyer hasn't completed its verification. Require a fundamental title warranty, free-of-encumbrance confirmation and duly executed transfers at Completion.

**SPA-N-016: Tax/IP open terms**
- **Seller:** Settled under the general regime.
- **Buyer wants:** A specific pre-Completion tax indemnity (tax deed) with a longer limitation period, plus stronger IP ownership and non-infringement warranties.
- **Recommendation:** Reject. There is no basis for treating these as settled, and the Ironquay and data incident issues show IP and compliance risks that a general regime doesn't address.

---

**Also unresolved**
- **Office lease (DD-007) and Mossvale (DD-009):** The letter doesn't say consent is required. I'd confirm against the underlying clauses and consider warranties or CPs if there is any doubt.
- **Funds flow:** Request the full draft, since it omits the bonuses and, apparently, the Riverlark payout.

I can turn these into a mark-up or issues list next if you'd like.
